info.title: OpenVibe.Mail API
info.description: Routes of OpenVibe.Mail as the OpenVibe contracts describe them (openvibe-contracts 0.330.0): each operation lists the capabilities it performs; a token for the service's audience must carry one of them unless the route is open. Generated by openvibe-contracts lib/openapi.js; do not edit.

get.summary: Read what arrived for a person's addresses: the addresses they own with their state and counts, and the metadata of a mask's, burner's or agent inbox's messages (sender, subject, time) plus the newest
get.description: **mail.messages.read** (first-party): Read what arrived for a person's addresses: the addresses they own with their state and counts, and the metadata of a mask's, burner's or agent inbox's messages (sender, subject, time) plus the newest verification code in a burner. Never a message body, and never another person's mail. The caller must act for the person (on_behalf_of), except a burner read with the one-time token its create call returned.

post.summary: Make and retire the addresses OpenVibe.Mail hands out for a person: a mask (a per-site address that delivers into their OpenVibe mailbox and nowhere else) and an agent inbox (<agent>.<user>@openvibe.e
post.description: **mail.addresses.write** (first-party): Make and retire the addresses OpenVibe.Mail hands out for a person: a mask (a per-site address that delivers into their OpenVibe mailbox and nowhere else) and an agent inbox (<agent>.<user>@openvibe.email). Turning a mask off makes its address bounce. The caller must act for the person (on_behalf_of); it never sends mail.

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
